charter_values_notes: Time horizon: The framework is built around anticipating irreversible, catastrophic outcomes (Loss of Control, superintelligence containment, prospective pre-training assessments), which is far-horizon thinking, though it is anchored to annual updates and near-term deployment cycles rather than century-scale planning. Transparency: It commits to published preparedness reports, model specs, evaluation methodology, disclosure of known testing limitations, whistleblower protections, and open weights as transparency — but with carve-outs for trade secrets, legal limits, security-sensitive threat details, and internal-use reports shared only as summaries with authorities. Risk tolerance: Notably permissive for a safety framework — v2.0 explicitly replaced 'Stop' with 'Develop with Mitigations' and 'Do not release' with 'Deploy with mitigations,' and it champions open-weight releases despite acknowledged unique abuse vectors; still, deployment at every level is gated on validated mitigations reducing risk to moderate-or-lower, so it is mitigation-gated rather than reckless. Democratic tendency: Mission rhetoric ('personal superintelligence to everyone,' 'putting power in people's hands') and open-weight distribution genuinely spread capability, and external experts/community can inspect models, but ultimate authority concentrates in the Chief AI Officer and Director of Alignment and Risk with only internal board oversight and no binding external accountability.
charter_values_self_notes: Long-horizon catastrophic, durable outcomes-led focus with 12-month updates; extensive preparedness reports/model spec but allows redactions for trade secrets/security; risk-averse with evaluations, heightened controls, proceed-only-with-validated-mitigations after loosening from Stop; mission to bring personal superintelligence to everyone and support open-weights ecosystem despite centralized Chief AI Officer/Board decisions.
